newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda and Sudan to meet over rebel disputes.
newsitem.headline: Uganda and Sudan to meet over rebel disputes.

text.p: Uganda and Sudan will hold talks mediated by Iran in Kampala this week, Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni said, accusing Khartoum of backing rebels in northern Uganda.
Museveni told a news conference late on Tuesday he did not expect any immediate progress at the talks as Sudan had not fulfilled its obligations under a previous agreement to end their dispute.
"I have agreed that talks should take place here," he said. "But of course we have not broken any ground with Mr (Hassan) al-Tourabi's people." Tourabi is Sudan's influential Islamic leader.

Museveni said Iran's foreign minister was expected in the Ugandan capital for the talks. Iran intervened in the row between Kampala and Khartoum in September and is supposed to verify accusations by both sides and sponsor agreements.
Uganda and Sudan broke diplomatic relations in April with both sides accusing the other of backing rebel movements.

Under a pact signed in Tehran in November Uganda and Sudan agreed to stop hostile propaganda campaigns, destroy rebel positions and supply centres, move all rebels and refugees at least 100 km (60 miles) inside their borders and encourage the voluntary repatriation of refugees from the two countries.
Museveni said Uganda was still intent on a military solution to a rebellion in northern Uganda it says is backed by Sudan.
"We must get a solution to al-Tourabi's blackmail, a military solution. I am not going to invade al-Tourabi. Al-Tourabi has enough enemies who will take care of him," he said.
Museveni referred to Tourabi rather than Sudan throughout the news conference. Sudan's President is Omar Hassan al-Bashir.
Uganda accuses Sudan of supporting the Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) rebels in the north. Sudan accuses Uganda of backing the Sudan Peoples' Liberation Army, the largest rebel group in southern Sudan.
Museveni said that in the last month his troops had killed at least 160 rebels in the north. He said rebels in the north or elsewhere in Uganda would be met by a mighty show of force.
"The rebels have one common characteristic. They don't want to work democratically. Anybody who takes that road will be crashed. I have never changed from that position," Museveni said.
